lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Owned the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards across two major releases and the on-call rotation that used them.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases, adding automated regression checks that shortened release cycles from 2 weeks to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: The résumé does not establish one primary target identity.
items.because: The reader must infer whether the focus is robotics software, ML engineering, or LLM and agent infrastructure.

items.says: Prioritize and order the roles, projects, and bullets around the chosen target role.
items.because: The most relevant and recent work should receive the strongest visual priority.

items.says: Make the concurrent M.S. and internship dates look intentional.
items.because: A reader may briefly wonder whether the overlapping dates are incorrect.

items.says: Use consistent punctuation and capitalization across bullets.
Make the code link clearly lead to relevant technical work.
items.because: An ambiguous link gives no indication that it contains substantial projects, and a recruiter may not investigate it.

items.says: Add a concise professional positioning line beneath the contact information.
items.because: The intended role is not obvious before the detailed bullets.

items.says: Consider adding relevant coursework or research that explains the M.S. technical direction.
items.because: The current degree does not show which target role it supports.

items.says: Consider replacing the B.S. location with a relevant academic distinction if space is needed.
items.because: The institution and degree matter more than the location.

items.says: Clarify what owning the dashboards involved and add an operational outcome.
items.because: The bullet shows responsibility but not whether the work improved reliability.

items.says: Clarify the relationship between the dashboards and the on-call rotation.
items.because: Saying the rotation used the dashboards is conceptually awkward as an accomplishment.

items.says: Specify the scope and measurement conditions of the latency improvement.
items.because: The reader cannot tell which endpoints or service were measured, or under what workload.

items.says: Clarify the 200 ms threshold and any cache freshness constraints.
items.because: The threshold's purpose and the caching tradeoff are not stated.

items.says: Specify what the automated regression checks tested and covered.
items.because: For an ML infrastructure role, “automated regression checks” is too broad.

items.says: Clarify how much of the shorter release cycle resulted from your automation.
items.because: The causal scope of the two-week-to-three-day result is unclear.

items.says: Split or shorten the fleet-migration bullet.
items.because: Its architecture, logging, onboarding, on-call, and backlog claims are hard to scan together.

items.says: Identify which action removed the nightly backlogs.
items.because: The bullet leaves the event queue, logging rewrite, and on-call work causally ambiguous.

items.says: Verify that the backlogs were eliminated rather than merely reduced.
items.because: “Removed” should be used only if it is literally accurate.

items.says: Check the rendered line wrapping around “on-call.”
items.because: The review flags a broken “on-call” line in the rendered document.

items.says: Explain what the triage branch is and what you personally owned.
items.because: “Triage branch” is company-specific, and the scope of your contribution is unclear.

items.says: Define the pending-case backlog, its baseline, and the operational benefit of reducing it.
items.because: The 68% result needs context showing what was reduced and why it mattered.

items.says: Define diagnostic accuracy and the evaluation setup for the 71%-to-79% result.
items.because: The experimental claim needs to be auditable, including whether cases were held out from tuning.

items.says: Explain the adapted base system, validated trajectories, and role of assistant-only loss masking.
items.because: The specialized terminology may not be clear outside the team.

items.says: Clarify how dynamic batching improved single-request edge inference.
items.because: Batching usually groups multiple requests, making the current wording appear contradictory.

items.says: Add baseline latency, workload, hardware, and relevant throughput or accuracy effects.
items.because: An inference-engineering reviewer needs more context to assess the 40% result.

items.says: The GRPO bullet is a grammatical fragment beginning with “Using.”
items.because: It reads like an experiment note rather than a finished accomplishment.

items.says: Explain what was trained and how the listed methods produced the latency improvement.
items.because: The mechanisms are named without a clear causal account of the changed behavior.

items.says: Give the 5% result a baseline and evidence of its significance.
items.because: It is unclear whether the effect was statistically or operationally meaningful.

items.says: Consider giving the GRPO latency result less prominence if its effect is small.
items.because: The other results may show stronger impact.

items.says: Show that the single-rollout choice meaningfully improved training.
items.because: The bullet states an implementation choice without evidence of its value.

items.says: Explain why one rollout per prompt was preferable in this setting.
items.because: A reviewer cannot tell whether it was an algorithmic improvement, a resource constraint, or a debugging workaround.

items.says: Quantify adoption or the operational effect of the runbook.
items.because: “Adopted them” does not show the impact on reviewers, escalation, or decisions.

items.says: Replace the AI-first practices bullet with a concrete technical or adoption result.
items.because: Its broad claims lack a defined practice, scope, measurable outcome, and evidence of adoption.

items.says: Replace the vague “AI-first” wording with what you built.
items.because: The phrase is generic and does not tell a technical reviewer what the work involved.

items.says: A drop from 900 ms to 600 ms is about 33%, not 50%.
items.because: The arithmetic error is a serious credibility problem.

items.says: Clarify whether both latency measurements used the same workload.
items.because: The comparison needs a consistent measurement basis.

items.says: Address cache-hit effects and the freshness or correctness of reused answers.
items.because: Caching and answer reuse can change volume or accuracy as well as latency.

items.says: The change from 71% to 83% is 12 percentage points, not a 12% relative increase.
items.because: The relative increase is approximately 17%.

items.says: Describe the benchmark size, repetition, and performance on unseen tasks.
items.because: The task-completion result needs evaluation context.

items.says: State the cost and correctness tradeoffs of partial-context retries.
items.because: Retries may add latency, tool calls, cost, or inconsistent actions.

items.says: Specify your role in designing, implementing, validating, or maintaining the metrics.
items.because: “Upstreamed” does not make individual ownership clear.

items.says: Clarify the significance and current extent of the metrics' upstream adoption.
items.because: The reader needs to understand their use in releases and whether the default-benchmark claim is literal.

items.says: Explain the injected degradation and what the evaluator score measured.
items.because: Without experimental context, the correlation looks like a disconnected number.

items.says: Specify the correlation measure and validation design.
items.because: It is unclear whether the trials were independent, the degradation was ordered, or the result was checked against human judgments.

items.says: State the consequences of the three pipeline defects.
items.because: The impact on benchmark validity, reproducibility, or production behavior is implicit.

items.says: Clarify what “fixed upstream” means and your role in the fixes.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether your fixes were merged or what remained in use.

items.says: Move Git out of Programming or omit it.
items.because: Git is expected rather than differentiating, and its current grouping looks less deliberate.

items.says: Reorganize ML and agent skills into technically meaningful groups.
items.because: The section should reinforce demonstrated technical areas.

items.says: Substantiate PyTorch and LoRA if they remain emphasized.
items.because: The experience does not explicitly establish direct PyTorch use or that the domain adapter used LoRA.

items.says: Make agent evaluation visibly central in the projects if it remains an emphasized skill.
items.because: The stated capability should be reinforced by the project evidence.

items.says: Add supporting Kubernetes experience or remove the skill.
items.because: Kubernetes appears only in skills and nowhere in the accomplishments.

items.says: Consider skills more directly supported by the experience.
items.because: Event-driven systems, CI/CD, inference optimization, observability, and evaluation may better reflect the bullets.
